topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Speeds Costs
explanation: The memory hierarchy optimizes system performance by structuring storage into tiered levels based on speed, size, and cost. Registers and L1/L2/L3 caches, being the fastest and most expensive SRAM, reside closest to the CPU. Main memory (DRAM) is slower and larger, while secondary storage (disk/SSD) provides the highest capacity at the lowest speed and cost. Caching strategies leverage temporal and spatial locality to predict data reuse, moving frequently accessed blocks into faster levels. This minimizes the average memory access time (AMAT) by maximizing the cache hit rate, effectively bridging the speed gap between the CPU and main memory.
